Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. # andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-rvv
make run-syscall
make run-coremark
make run-dhrystone
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `syscall-*`, `coremark-*` and
`dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

-include ../../Make.var

CC:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc
OBJDUMP:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)objdump
GDB:=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gdb
CFLAGS:= -march=rv$(XLEN)gc_zicbom_xandes $(OPT_LEVEL) -g
ACE_FLAGS:= -Wa,-mace=lib/libacetool.eca

TARGETS := ace_test
DUMPS := $(TARGETS:=.dump)

all: $(TARGETS) $(DUMPS)

lib/libacetool.eca: test_inst.ace
	$(COPILOT) $< -a --keep-lib-src --keep-unused-resource

$(TARGETS): %: %.c lib/libacetool.eca
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ $(VSIM_FILES) $(CFLAGS) $(ACE_FLAGS) $(VSIM_FLAGS)

ace_dbg: ace_test.c lib/libacetool.eca
	$(CC) $(filter %.c,$^) -o $@ $(VSIM_FILES) $(CFLAGS) $(ACE_FLAGS) $(VSIM_FLAGS) -DWAIT_FOR_DEBUGGER

$(DUMPS): %.dump: %
	$(OBJDUMP) $< -d -Mace=lib/libacetool.eca > $@

install: all ace_dbg
	@mkdir -p $(INSTALL_PREFIX)
	@cp -f ace_test ace_test.dump ace_dbg $(INSTALL_PREFIX)/

clean:
	- rm -rf ace_test *.o *.dump lib include

.PHONY: clean all install

run: ace_test
	$(SIMULATOR_BIN) $^

# ------------ Below is for testing GDB on ACR and ACM ----------------

GREEN=\033[0;32m
RED=\033[0;31m
NC=\033[0m # No Color

lib/libacedbg.eca: test_inst.ace
	$(COPILOT) $< -a --keep-lib-src --keep-unused-resource

dbg: ace_dbg lib/libacedbg.eca
	-rm -f gdb.txt
	cp lib/libacedbg.eca $(ICEMAN)/
	$(VSIM) $< --jdtm-rbb-port 9104 &
	@sleep 10
	cd $(ICEMAN) && ./ICEman -Z v5 -I virtual_dmi.cfg --ace-conf core0=libacedbg.eca &
	@sleep 5
	$(GDB) -x test_ace.gdb -q
	@sleep 10
	python verify.py gdb.txt;  status=$$?; \
	if [ $$status -eq 0 ]; then \
	    echo -e "\n$(GREEN)succeeded$(NC)\n"; \
	else \
	    echo -e "\n$(RED)failed$(NC)\n"; \
	fi
	@sleep 2
	-pkill -f $(VSIM)
	-pkill -f ICEman

.PHONY: clean all dbg
This Makefile is for AST540. If you use AST533/530, or even older version, plz see Makefile.ast533

- COPILOT 730+ and AST540+
- COPILOT 720+ and AST530+

You have to set several Paths in Makefile.

`VSIM`, `ICEMAN`, `COPILOT`, `ANDES_TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX`

```sh
VSIM=../../../buildace/sim_d45 make run
```

```sh
make dbg
```

```sh
make -f Makefile.ast533 dbg
```

## Demo Code

Two ACERVV instructions are implemented in `ace-rvv.ace`, corresponding to the following two test cases:

### abs_diff
Uses the ACERVV `vabd_vx` instruction to accelerate signed absolute difference computation.

### complex_mul
Uses the ACERVV widening instruction `vwcmul` to accelerate signed complex number multiplication computation.
Note that this is just a demo and does not handle overflow, so use with caution.

### vqwmacc
Do multiply-add fusion on quad-widening and double-widening vector operands.

When measuring cycles for RVV or ACERVV instructions, remember to use the `fence` instruction to ensure all operations are completed, since the VPU retires out-of-order relative to the scalar pipeline.

## Steps

Set the COPILOT and toolchain paths in `../../Make.var`.

Then run:
```sh
make
```

Add the path to `lib/libaceasim.a` to the AndesCycle `build/build.ninja` file's `libaceasim = ` field.

Rebuild:

```sh
ninja sim sim_py
```

Then you can run this demo:


# ---- Shared configuration (can be overridden) ----

# Path to your andesim checkout, already built with scripts/build_all.sh.
ANDESIM ?= /home/nick/work/andesim

# Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `andesim doctor` reports).
XLEN ?= 64
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?= /local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d/bin/riscv$(XLEN)-unknown-elf-

COPILOT ?= 

# Cycle-accurate engine for --mode cycle / hybrid.
# See `andesim list engines` for what is available.
ENGINE ?= vsim:ax45mpv_premium

# Compiler optimization flag
OPT_LEVEL ?= -O2

# Extra flags for every andesim invocation, e.g. --log-level 1
ANDESIM_FLAGS ?=

# ---- Do not touch the followings ----

ANDESIM_BIN := $(ANDESIM)/andesim
RUNTIME := $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime

CC := $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc
OBJDUMP := $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)objdump

# One ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid: link against the andesim runtime
# (UART stdio + SimControl exit, no semihosting). -B also puts the runtime's
# include/ on the search path, so <andesim/ROI.h> works.
CFLAGS := -march=rv$(XLEN)gc -mabi=lp64d $(OPT_LEVEL) \
          -B $(RUNTIME) -specs=andesim.specs

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/syscall \
           demo/coremark demo/dhrystone

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

rvv-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/rvv $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

run     run one simulation (the default: 'run' may be omitted)
  fast      QEMU only -- functional, full speed
  cycle     one cycle-accurate engine, from reset
  hybrid    QEMU fast-forwards, then vsim measures the ROI

  --mode fast|cycle|hybrid    REQUIRED  which mode to run
  --trigger marker|pc         REQUIRED for hybrid  the ROI delimiter
    --pc-start <sym|0x>       REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI start boundary
    --pc-end <sym|0x>         REQUIRED for --trigger pc  ROI end boundary
  --engine <id>               pick an engine, e.g. vsim:ax45mpv_premium (default: the sole one)
  --mem-size <spec>           guest RAM, e.g. 256M / 2G (hybrid: max 2G; fast: QEMU -m; cycle: ignored)
  --dry-run                   print the exact engine command(s) and exit, running nothing (fast/cycle/hybrid)

# RVV intrinsics need V in the arch string; the later -march wins.

	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -march=rv$(XLEN)gcv $< -o $@

	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode fast $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode cycle --engine $(ENGINE) $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine $(ENGINE) $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode hybrid --trigger pc \

run: rvv-fast rvv-cycle rvv-hybrid-marker rvv-hybrid-pc

# Collect outputs for the custom target
  set(_verilated_outputs
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libverilated.a"
    "${_config_header}"
  )

  # Step 3: Optionally build libaceasim.a from stubs
  # LIBACEASIM_PATH can be:
  #   "stubs/<N>"            → build from stubs/<N>/ directory
  #   "/absolute/path/..."   → pre-built; no build step, just link
  #   ""                     → no libaceasim
  if(LIBACEASIM_PATH)
    set(_asim_prepare_stamp "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/.asim_prepare.stamp")
    set(_asim_lib_in_series "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/${CPU_SERIES}/libaceasim.a")

    add_custom_command(
      OUTPUT "${_asim_prepare_stamp}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E rm -rf "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/${CPU_SERIES}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_directory "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/${CPU_SERIES}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/${CPU_SERIES}"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/ver.c" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/ver.c"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/makefile" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/makefile"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch "${_asim_prepare_stamp}"
      DEPENDS "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/${CPU_SERIES}/ace.v" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/makefile" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/stubs/ver.c"
      COMMENT "Preparing aceasim sources for ${CPU_NAME}"
    )

    add_custom_command(
      OUTPUT "${_asim_lib_in_series}"
      COMMAND make
        "INCDIR=${CONFIG_DIR}"
        "${CPU_SERIES}"
        "verilator=${VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE}"
        "CXX=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}"
      WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
      DEPENDS "${_asim_prepare_stamp}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
      COMMENT "Building stub libaceasim for ${CPU_NAME}"
    )

    add_custom_command(
      OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a"
      COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different "${_asim_lib_in_series}" "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a"
      DEPENDS "${_asim_lib_in_series}"
      COMMENT "Staging libaceasim.a for ${CPU_NAME}"
    )
    list(APPEND _verilated_outputs "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a")
  endif()

  # Custom target for this CPU's verilated artifacts
  add_custom_target(verilated_${CPU_NAME} DEPENDS ${_verilated_outputs})
endfunction()

/* HVM through the bus subordinate port -- across the hybrid handoff.
 *
 * The HVM (High-Bandwidth Vector Memory) is the vector unit's private
 * 256 KB SRAM at 0x90000000, 2 banks (bank = address bit 17). Unlike
 * the ILM/DLM it has no enable CSR and no hart-local address: its one
 * window IS the bus subordinate port. So every access here is a plain
 * SCALAR load/store -- on the RTL it leaves the hart's bus master port,
 * is routed by the interconnect, and enters the HVM through that
 * subordinate port, the same port an external master would use
 * (demo/hvm_dma makes that literal).
 *
 * QEMU phase (before the ROI):
 *   - scalar-fill the whole 256 KB with a runtime-computed pattern
 *   - sanity: read head and tail back
 *
 * vsim ROI:
 *   - scalar-read every 64th word plus the words a bank-split bug would
 *     hit (bank0 head/tail, bank1 head/tail; bank = address bit 17),
 *     compare; prints HVM_SLV_OK / HVM_SLV_BAD
 *
 * The pattern reaches the RTL's HVM SRAM only via the sidecar transport
 * (plugin drain -> <state>.hvm -> vsim backdoor load); QEMU's HVM RAM
 * is not backed by the shared DRAM mmap.
 *
 * Geometry matches vsim:ax45mpv_premium: HVM 256 KB at 0x90000000.
 */

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <andesim/ROI.h>

#define HVM_BASE   0x90000000u
#define HVM_BYTES  262144u
#define HVM_WORDS  (HVM_BYTES / 4u)
#define STRIDE     64u

static inline uint32_t pat(uint32_t i) { return i * 2654435761u + 0x5B33u; }

static uint32_t check_word(uint32_t i)
{
  volatile uint32_t *hvm = (volatile uint32_t *) (uintptr_t) HVM_BASE;
  return hvm[i] != pat(i);
}

/* ROI body, noinline and non-static so --trigger pc can name it. */
__attribute__((noinline)) int hslv_check(void)
{
  uint32_t bad = 0, checked = 0;

  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < HVM_WORDS; i += STRIDE) {
    bad += check_word(i);
    checked++;
  }
  /* Bank boundary and tails: bank0 = words [0, 32768), bank1 = the rest. */
  static const uint32_t spots[3] = {HVM_WORDS / 2u - 1u, HVM_WORDS / 2u,
                                    HVM_WORDS - 1u};
  for (int s = 0; s < 3; s++) {
    bad += check_word(spots[s]);
    checked++;
  }

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

AndesCycle (vsim) — a Verilator-based cycle-accurate simulator for Andes RISC-V CPU cores. This workspace builds customer-facing Docker images containing the simulator, toolchain, and demo programs.

**Git structure**: Main repo with two submodules — `vsim` (branch: develop) for the simulator, `vsim-demo` (branch: main) for demo/test programs.

## Build Commands

### Docker image build (primary workflow)
```bash
./build.sh {dev|runtime|bin}
```
- `dev` — full development environment (RTL hidden, source visible)
- `runtime` — runtime with Python pipeline visualization tools
- `bin` — binary-only, minimal footprint

### Local simulator build (inside vsim/)
```bash
cd vsim
./configure --builddir build --install-prefix ./
cd build && ninja sim
```
Key configure flags: `--no-verilator` (skip RTL compilation), `--debug` (enable Verilator trace)

### Demo programs (inside vsim-demo/)
```bash
make run -C vsim-demo          # Build and run all demos
make rvv -C vsim-demo          # Build specific demo (hello, dhrystone, rvv, cpp, syscall, etc.)
```

## Testing

Tests run inside Docker containers:
```bash
docker run \
  -v $PWD/run-tests.sh:/work/run-tests.sh \
  -v $PWD/toolchain:/work/toolchain \
  -v $PWD/vsim-demo:/work/vsim-demo \
  localhost/andescycle-dev:TAG \
  bash /work/run-tests.sh
```

Test suite (`run-tests.sh`) checks: file existence (no leaked Verilog sources), `--version` output, pipeline visualization (konata.py), and demo program execution.

## Architecture

### Simulator core (vsim/src/)
- **SystemC/TLM-2.0** module architecture with cycle-accurate timing
- `main.cpp` — entry point
- `simulator.hpp` — core simulator, ELF loading via LIEF library
- `cpu_wrappers/` — per-CPU Verilated module wrappers (one per CPU in config.yaml)
- `platform/` — TLM-2.0 platform: interconnect (AXI/AHB), memory, JTAG DTM, sim_control
- `pybind11.cpp` — Python module binding for pipeline analysis
- `signals/` — CPU-specific signal definitions

### Supported CPUs (config.yaml)
Each CPU entry maps a binary name to its RTL package, C++ wrapper class, and config. CPUs: ax45mpv_premium, ax65, d45, d45_se, nx45v_plain, d23, d25fse.

### Build system
Python `configure` script generates `build.ninja` from Jinja2 templates + `config.yaml`. Verilator compiles RTL → C++, then clang++ compiles everything.

### Python tools (vsim/tools/)
- `konata.py` — pipeline visualization
- `andes45.py` / `andes23.py` — CPU-specific analysis
- `functrace.py` — function tracing

## Code Quality

- **C++20**, compiled with clang/clang++, `-O2`, `-march=x86-64-v3`
- **clang-format**: 80-column limit (config in `vsim/.clang-format`)
- **clang-tidy**: bugprone, cert, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, readability checks (config in `vsim/.clang-tidy`)
- **Pre-commit hooks** (`vsim/.pre-commit-config.yaml`): clang-format, black, mypy, shellcheck
- **Python**: formatted with black, type-checked with mypy

## Key Dependencies

- `pybind11.cpp` — Python module binding for pipeline analysis
- `signals/` — CPU-specific signal definitions

### Supported CPUs (config.yaml)
Each CPU entry maps a binary name to its RTL package, C++ wrapper class, and config. CPUs: ax45mpv_premium, ax65, d45, d45_se, nx45v_plain, d23, d25fse.

### Build system
Python `configure` script generates `build.ninja` from Jinja2 templates + `config.yaml`. Verilator compiles RTL → C++, then clang++ compiles everything.

### Python tools (vsim/tools/)
- `konata.py` — pipeline visualization
- `andes45.py` / `andes23.py` — CPU-specific analysis
- `functrace.py` — function tracing

## Code Quality

- **C++20**, compiled with clang/clang++, `-O2`, `-march=x86-64-v3`
- **clang-format**: 80-column limit (config in `vsim/.clang-format`)
- **clang-tidy**: bugprone, cert, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, readability checks (config in `vsim/.clang-tidy`)
- **Pre-commit hooks** (`vsim/.pre-commit-config.yaml`): clang-format, black, mypy, shellcheck
- **Python**: formatted with black, type-checked with mypy

input.content:
---
name: ace-in-andesim-bringup
description: How to run Andes ACE (custom-extension) demos under andesim fast/cycle, and the copilot/eca/agent version blockers.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Goal: make andesim-demo run ACE demos (ref: /local/nick/vsim-demo-new/demo/ace, ace-rvv) in fast (QEMU) and cycle (vsim) modes. Started 2026-07-11.

**Pipeline per demo**: `copilot <x>.ace` -> `lib/libacetool.eca` (assembler encodings) + `include/ace_user.h` (C intrinsics) + `lib/libacesim.so` (SID C++ model). Compile: `gcc <src> -march=rv64gc..._xandes -Wa,-mace=lib/libacetool.eca -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. The andesim vplat runtime links fine with ACE ELFs.

**eca format is version-matched to the assembler** (root cause of "format error"):
- Old/compatible eca = tiny file, plaintext `//VERSION://DATE://SHA` header + AES-128-CBC (key `58b5d7a9973581c7b4ef9e9fc3963d26`, embedded in `as`) over a compact encoding array. ALL installed assemblers (AST540/541/542/550) accept ONLY this.
- The engineering copilot `/home/nick/work/copilot/copilot/build/src/copilot` (7.3.0) emits a NEW eca = AES-CBC (key `_COPILOT_SECRET_`) over the FULL ace-description JSON (~256KB). NO installed assembler reads it -> "format error". Needs a newer `as` than exists here.
- Working copilot for eca: `/local/ycc738/copilot/bin/copilot` (emits old-format eca, AST541 loads it). Older `/local/ycc738/COPILOT_726_*` emits `libacetool.so` instead.

Done with the probe. Here is what I found.

## Answer
`--` passthrough is enough to *inject* the ACE settings, but it is **not** enough to actually run the ACE demos. Fast mode is blocked on a missing QEMU "ACE agent" library, and cycle mode needs the vsim engine rebuilt (not a runtime flag). I did get the compile step working and one ACE demo built against the andesim runtime.

## What works now
- **Compile**: I set up `andesim-demo/demo/ace` (copied `test_inst.ace` + `ace_test.c`), generated the ACE files, and built `ace_test.elf` with the andesim vplat runtime (`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`). The runtime links ACE ELFs fine.
- **Passthrough plumbing**: `./andesim run --mode fast <elf> -- -cpu andes-ax46mpv,xandesace=on,xandesacelib=<agent>.so` correctly appends a second `-cpu` and QEMU uses it (confirmed by `--dry-run`).

## The blockers (real root causes, not quick-fix material)

1. **copilot ↔ assembler version mismatch (eca).** The copilot you pointed me at (`/home/nick/work/copilot/.../copilot`, 7.3.0) writes a *new* `libacetool.eca` (an encrypted full-JSON, ~256 KB). **No installed assembler reads it** - AST540, AST541, AST542, AST550 all say `format error`. They only accept the *old* small eca format. I found a working generator: `/local/ycc738/copilot/bin/copilot` produces the old format, and AST541 loads it. I used that to build the ELF.

2. **Fast mode (QEMU) has no ACE agent.** With `xandesace=on`, QEMU `dlopen`s the lib and calls a C ABI `ace_agent_register/version/run_insn/get_register` at version **102** (`qemu/target/riscv/ace-helper.h`). copilot only gives us the **C++** SID model (`libacesim.so`) or fastsim model (`libacefsim.so`) - neither exports those C symbols, so QEMU aborts with `register failed`. A C shim wrapping the SID model must be compiled into the agent `.so`. No such shim or prebuilt agent exists anywhere in your trees - **ACE has only ever run on vsim here, never QEMU.**

3. **Cycle mode (vsim) is a rebuild, not passthrough.** Per the ace-rvv README, you must generate `libaceasim.a` (`copilot --gen-asim`), wire it into vsim `config.yaml` (`libaceasim_path`), and `ninja sim`. The engine binary itself changes. (The 7.3.0 copilot's `--gen-asim` also errored on `test_inst.ace` with an internal RTL-gen bug.)

Also note: **andesim itself has zero ACE awareness today** - no eca/agent handling in its source. So this is genuine integration work.

I saved the full detail (paths, keys, header-staging steps, ABI) to memory so we don't re-derive it.

**eca format is version-matched to the assembler** (root cause of "format error"):
- Old/compatible eca = tiny file, plaintext `//VERSION://DATE://SHA` header + AES-128-CBC (key `58b5d7a9973581c7b4ef9e9fc3963d26`, embedded in `as`) over a compact encoding array. ALL installed assemblers (AST540/541/542/550) accept ONLY this.

- Working copilot for eca: `/local/ycc738/copilot/bin/copilot` (emits old-format eca, AST541 loads it). Older `/local/ycc738/COPILOT_726_*` emits `libacetool.so` instead.

Also pass `--cxx-path /usr/bin/g++`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --mem-size contract: one model-neutral flag, per-model semantics, plus the
# hybrid V-scratch boundary.
#
#   fast:   forwards --mem-size verbatim to QEMU's `-m`; QEMU itself validates
#           its DRAM ceiling (this AE350 build tops out at 16 GiB). A non-whole-
#           MiB size is rejected by the driver first.
#   hybrid: sizes the shared mmap (= QEMU backend = vsim window). The driver
#           reserves ONE V-scratch page ABOVE program RAM, so the usable window
#           is the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM window MINUS that page. Exactly 2G therefore
#           overflows and is rejected; 2047M is the largest whole-MiB size that
#           fits. See driver/shm.cpp max_program_mem_bytes().
#   cycle:  validate-only (the engine always models its full DRAM window).
#   --mmap-size stays a hidden alias of --mem-size.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"        # engine-portable (fast/cycle)
MELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"        # carries ROI markers (hybrid)
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (make -C tests/fixtures)"
[ -f "$MELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $MELF (make -C tests/fixtures)"

# hybrid <SIZE> <want-rc> then per-line assertions; runs the command ONCE.
hy() { "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" --log-level 1 "$@" "$MELF" </dev/null 2>&1; }

# --- fast: pass-through to QEMU -m -------------------------------------------
# 1G accepted, program still runs.
expect 0 'hello from vplat' "$BIN" run --mode fast --mem-size 1G "$ELF"
# QEMU's own ceiling: this AE350 build refuses more than 16 GiB (FAILURE case).
expect 1 'Cannot model more than 16GB RAM' "$BIN" run --mode fast --mem-size 32G "$ELF"
# A size that is not a whole MiB: driver rejects before spawning (FAILURE case).
expect 2 'whole MiB' "$BIN" run --mode fast --mem-size 1000 "$ELF"

# --- hybrid: sized shared mmap, capped at the 2 GiB window minus V-scratch ---
# BOUNDARY (FAILURE): exactly 2G overflows by the one reserved V-scratch page;
# the cap fires BEFORE any mmap file is allocated.
out=$(hy --mem-size 2G); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 2 ] || fail "hybrid --mem-size 2G rc=$rc (want 2):"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "AE350 DRAM window" || fail "hybrid 2G: missing cap message:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" \
  && fail "hybrid 2G must fail BEFORE allocating the mmap:"$'\n'"$out"

# BOUNDARY (ACCEPT): 2047M is the largest whole-MiB size that fits; the shared
# mmap rounds to 2.0 GiB and the run completes with a cycle figure.
out=$(hy --mem-size 2047M); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid --mem-size 2047M rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap 2.0 GiB" \
  || fail "hybrid 2047M: mmap status should show 2.0 GiB:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -Eq "\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles" || fail "hybrid 2047M: no cycle figure:"$'\n'"$out"

# mid-size: mmap sized to the request, run completes.
out=$(hy --mem-size 256M); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid --mem-size 256M rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap 256.0 MiB" \
  || fail "hybrid 256M: mmap status should show 256.0 MiB:"$'\n'"$out"

# the retired --mmap-size spelling still works (hidden alias).
out=$(hy --mmap-size 192M); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "--mmap-size alias rc=$rc:"$'\n'"$out"
echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap 192.0 MiB" \
  || fail "alias: mmap status should show 192.0 MiB:"$'\n'"$out"

# --- cycle: validated, declared a no-op, run still passes --------------------
expect 0 'nothing to size' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 64M "$ELF"

ok "--mem-size contract (fast forwards to QEMU ceiling; hybrid capped at 2G-Vscratch: 2G rejected, 2047M max; cycle no-op; alias)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# --mem-size demo: different sizes / boundary / negative, across fast|cycle|hybrid.
# Cheap cases only (validation + print-memmap): no vsim spawn except the two
# tagged [RUN] fast cases at the end.
set -uo pipefail
cd /home/nick/work/andesim
BIN=./build/andesim
ELF=tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf     # engine-portable
ENG=vsim:ax45mpv_premium

row() { printf '%-7s %-9s %-4s %s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4"; }
hdr() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$1"; printf '%-7s %-9s %-4s %s\n' MODE SPEC RC 'KEY OUTPUT LINE'; }

# hybrid sizing via print-memmap (no engine spawn): grab the DRAM line or the error.
hy_size() {
  local spec=$1
  local out; out=$($BIN run --mode hybrid --print-memmap --engine "$ENG" --mem-size "$spec" 2>&1); local rc=$?
  local line
  if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then line=$(echo "$out" | awk '/^DRAM/{print "DRAM "$2" .. "$3"  size="$4}')
  else line=$(echo "$out" | grep -m1 -i 'mem-size\|invalid\|exceeds\|must be'); fi
  row hybrid "$spec" "$rc" "$line"
}

# generic: run any mode, show first salient stderr line (or the success marker).
gen() {
  local mode=$1 spec=$2 want=$3; shift 3
  local out; out=$("$@" 2>&1); local rc=$?
  local line; line=$(echo "$out" | grep -m1 -iE "$want" | head -c 120)
  [ -z "$line" ] && line=$(echo "$out" | grep -m1 -iE 'mem-size|invalid|must be|whole MiB|exceeds|Cannot model|nothing to size' | head -c 120)
  row "$mode" "$spec" "$rc" "$line"
}

hdr "A. different valid sizes (hybrid: DRAM window sized to --mem-size)"
for s in 64M 256M 1G 1.5G 131072K 2047M; do hy_size "$s"; done

hdr "B. boundary (hybrid cap = 2 GiB - 4 KiB V-scratch; largest whole MiB = 2047M)"
for s in 2047M 2048M 2G 3G; do hy_size "$s"; done

hdr "C. negative / invalid (parse rejects before any spawn)"
gen cycle 0     'must be'                 $BIN run --mode cycle  --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 0   "$ELF"
gen cycle 0M    'must be'                 $BIN run --mode cycle  --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 0M  "$ELF"
gen cycle -5    'invalid'                 $BIN run --mode cycle  --engine "$ENG" --mem-size -5  "$ELF"
gen cycle abc   'invalid'                 $BIN run --mode cycle  --engine "$ENG" --mem-size abc "$ELF"
gen cycle 1G2   'invalid'                 $BIN run --mode cycle  --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 1G2 "$ELF"
gen cycle 10X   'invalid'                 $BIN run --mode cycle  --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 10X "$ELF"

hdr "D. fast pass-through to QEMU -m (whole-MiB rule; QEMU 16 GiB ceiling)"
gen fast  1000  'whole MiB'               $BIN run --mode fast --mem-size 1000 "$ELF"
gen fast  0.5M  'whole MiB'               $BIN run --mode fast --mem-size 0.5M "$ELF"
gen fast  32G   'Cannot model'            $BIN run --mode fast --mem-size 32G  "$ELF"   # [RUN] spawns QEMU, dies

hdr "E. cycle: validated but nothing to size (still runs)"
# validation-only demo (no spawn): show the warn by pairing a bad+good; good spawns vsim so skip.
gen cycle 64M-parse-ok 'nothing to size'  $BIN run --mode cycle --engine "$ENG" --mem-size 64M --dry-run "$ELF"

hdr "F. accepted + actually runs [RUN spawns QEMU]"
gen fast  64M   'hello from vplat'         $BIN run --mode fast --mem-size 64M "$ELF"
echo

content.text:
Live demo done. Report while the end-to-end run finishes in the background.

## `andesim --mem-size` behavior demo

**Contract:** one flag, three modes. `parse_size` (regex `\d+(.\d+)?[KMGT]?`, case-insensitive) is shared; each mode then applies its own rule.

### A. Different valid sizes (hybrid DRAM window tracks `--mem-size`)
| spec | bytes | DRAM window | V-scratch |
|---|---|---|---|
| `64M` | 64 MiB | `0x0..0x3ffffff` | `0x4000000` |
| `256M` | 256 MiB | `0x0..0xfffffff` | `0x10000000` |
| `1G` | 1 GiB | `0x0..0x3fffffff` | above it |
| `1.5G` | 1536 MiB | decimal accepted | above it |
| `131072K` | 128 MiB | K unit works | above it |
| `2047M` | 2047 MiB | largest that fits | `0x7ff00000` |

### B. Boundary (hybrid cap = 2 GiB - 4 KiB V-scratch page)
- `2047M` -> **accepted** (largest whole MiB; the 4 KiB scratch page sits just under 2 GiB)
- `2048M` / `2G` / `3G` -> **rejected rc=2**, `exceeds the AE350 DRAM window (2G minus the V-scratch reservation)`, and it fails **before** any mmap file is allocated.

### C. Negative / invalid (rejected at parse, no engine spawn, rc=2)
- `0`, `0M` -> `must be > 0`
- `-5`, `abc`, `1G2`, `10X` -> `expected <number>[K|M|G|T]`

### D. Fast = pass-through to QEMU `-m`
- `1000` (bytes), `0.5M` -> rc=2 `QEMU's -m takes whole MiB; round to a multiple of 1M` (driver rejects first)
- `32G` -> forwarded, QEMU's own ceiling fires: rc=1 `Cannot model more than 16GB RAM`
- `64M` -> accepted, runs: `hello from vplat`

### E. Cycle = validate-only
- Bad specs still rejected (rc=2). Valid specs: rc=0 with warn `the cycle engine models its full DRAM window; nothing to size`.

**Two subtleties worth noting:**
1. Only **fast** enforces whole-MiB (QEMU `-m` limitation). Hybrid accepts non-whole-MiB (`1.5G`, `2047M` internally rounds the mmap) - the sizing is byte-granular.
2. Negatives never reach an engine - `parse_size` gates everything up front, so the failure cost is ~milliseconds regardless of mode.

The heavy end-to-end test (real vsim at `2047M` and `256M`) is running in the background (ID `bzsu8q4bi`); I'll report its result when it lands.
